Hannah / Evan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed Proof-of-Value (PoV) approach so we can align on scope, success criteria, ownership and timeline. Please confirm or flag changes.

Summary of goals
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + retrieval-augmented responses for agent assist.
- Key metrics you asked for: p95 generation latency < 350ms (for 512-token responses), retrieval precision AUC > 0.85, end-to-end session reliability > 99.8%.

Proposed PoV (4 weeks) — high level
1) Week 0 (prep): grant test account + access to a small snapshot of support docs (you provided sample dataset).
2) Week 1 (integration): SDK integration (Python/Node) + sample calls to /v1/generate (streaming) and /v1/embeddings. We’ll provide a lightweight sample repo.
3) Week 2 (eval): run retrieval/embedding evals on your sample set; measure quality & tune prompts.
4) Week 3 (performance): load test, streaming stability, KV cache warmup and latency profiling.
5) Week 4 (wrap): deliver success report and runbook; decide next steps (Dedicated vs Hosted).

Technical notes / ask from FinexCo
- We’ll need an example dataset (1000 docs) and a set of 50 evaluation prompts.
- Confirm if you require encrypted-at-rest integration with your KMS (we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments).
- Do you want function/tool calling for RAG orchestration (i.e., call external search/DB from the model) or keep it simple for the PoV?

Ownership
- Redwood AE: Marissa Cole (me) — program owner / commercial lead.
- Redwood SE: Rafael Mendes — solution architecture, rollout/observability.
- Redwood Tech Lead (integration): Dev Patel — SDK + sample repo, test keys, perf runs.

Deliverables attached: finexco_pov_statement.pdf (scope + SOW), integration_summary.xlsx (test dataset checklist), sdk_migration_guide.md (sample snippets).

Next steps
- Please confirm success criteria and whether function-calling is in-scope by Friday.
- Can we lock a kickoff (30m) next Monday 11/22 10:00 AM PT? I’ll send calendar invites once you confirm.

We prefer SSE if supported. Also want to confirm p95 measurement methodology (end-to-end vs server-side token generation only).

2) Data handling: we need confirmation that test logs from PoV will not be retained beyond 30 days and that we can opt out of storage for any PII. SOC 2 report would be appreciated.

3) Credentials & test keys: please provide ephemeral test credentials for the PoV environment. We want to run some smoke tests before the kickoff.

4) Success metric nuance: for embeddings, our internal baseline AUC on our model is 0.82 — to be a win we want >= 0.86 on the sample set (slightly higher than the number in your email).

Finally — is a lightweight MSA amendment required before we run infrastructure tests? Our procurement prefers a short POV addendum rather than a full contract.

Marissa / Rafael — quick technical confirmation and ETA below. TL;DR: all feasible; I’ll have a sample repo + creds by EOD Monday (11/22).

Streaming: we support both SSE and WebSocket streaming. For in-agent partial updates where the agent UI expects text-chunk-by-chunk, SSE is simplest (no extra handshake) and is what we recommend for browser-based agent UIs. WebSockets are available if FinexCo wants full-duplex. Example (pseudo):
- HTTP SSE: GET /v1/generate?stream=true (server sends event: data: <chunk>)
- WebSocket: ws://realtime.redwood/api/... with token handshake.

Latency measurement: p95 we typically report server-side generation time (token generation) + network median. For customer-facing p95 we recommend running an end-to-end synthetic test from your agent host (we can provide a k6 script). We’ll target <350ms p95 for 512 tokens in PoV environment; if we see higher we’ll adjust batching and KV cache warmup.

Embeddings & quality: we’ll run a baseline comparison against your sample set. Initial tuning (prompt/template + embedding model variant) typically takes 2–5 business days to reach best AUC. Reaching 0.86 is achievable on many datasets; we’ll set up an evaluation harness and report ROC/AUC daily.

Function / tool calling: for PoV we recommend enabling function calling in a limited mode (single external search call) to validate orchestration. Full-scale RAG pipelines can come post-PoV.

Deliverables and ETA
- Monday EOD (11/22): sample repo with minimal Python + Node examples (SSE streaming example included), ephemeral API key and smoke test instructions.
- Wednesday (11/24): first embedding evaluation report.
- Following week: perf runs and final success report.

I’ve attached sdk_migration_guide.md with a short SSE snippet. I’ll create the Drive folder and add the k6 script for end-to-end latency tests.

—
